chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Do not eat in vessels made of silver, nor in vessels that are silvered."

key_terms.مُفَضَّضَةٍ: silvered (coated with a layer of silver)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating from silver dishes in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits eating from silver or silvered vessels, a ruling that Shia jurists often link to the concept of *israf* (extravagance) and the distinction between gold and silver for adornment versus currency. This prohibition is frequently discussed in the context of *al-khamr* (wine) or general dining etiquette, emphasizing modesty in daily habits as a reflection of spiritual purity.
